shipped_rows.title_o: The Origin of the State: Land Productivity or Appropriability? A Comment
shipped_rows.outcome_quote: Computational: The data and code provided by MMP closely reproduce the main results presented in their Table 1 (see our Table 1). Any discrepancies we have found are presented in red text; these discrepancies are small and do not change the qualitative interpretation of the results. || Robustness: Concurrently testing the cereal cultivation and land productivity claims leads to slightly less statistical significance, on average, than the published article (Table 2). Removing the inherited 1-5 scale of the dependent variable (hierarchy) finds that cereal production is not as effective at moving across all levels of hierarchy compared to the more general claim (Table 3 and 4). The statistical significance of Claim 1 is sensitive to the removal of the top 3% of observations outliers (Table 7). Correction of sample restrictions (which keeps only areas where cereals are the dominant crops) results in less statistically significant evidence for Claim 1 (Table 10).
